audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict penultimate (penultimate stress) with word domain rests on Gault 1979 §1.3 p. 54, a dedicated phonemics article on exactly this variety; the quotation is verified verbatim in the text and PDF we hold ( page 60 = printed p. 54), and the same article independently uses penultimate stress as a syllable-count diagnostic (§1.4.2) and states that suffixes/enclitic pronouns shift stress rightward while monosyllabic particles are extrametrical — all consistent with the record. Glottolog's other descriptive items are morphosyntax/discourse (Gault 1999 held, silent on stress), and Ingilan's field survey confirms no grammar or other phonology of Bangingi exists, so the best available source is. sources.quote: No statement on stress. Reports that Sama Bangingi' vowels 'have for the most part reduced to 5' with schwa surviving only marginally (e.g. word-initial in nsa', citing Gault p.c. 2018 and Manga bissara 1993) — relevant only because the Pallesen-derived schwa-penult stress exception (see wishlist) would have little scope in Bangingi.
